themes_detail.label: Tree hazards spike dramatically
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints jumped to 14 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.8 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% spike (z-score: 12.65)—signaling potential safety hazards and infrastructure damage across the district.
evidence: 14 overgrown tree/branch complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly average (700% increase)
z-score of 12.65 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Timing suggests weather event or seasonal cycle requiring investigation
reporting_angles: Are fallen branches blocking roads or threatening homes? Interview affected residents and PARKS.
Has storm damage or heavy rain this week triggered the spike? Cross-check with weather data.
Is Parks Department maintenance falling behind? Request trim schedules and staffing levels.

themes_detail.label: Street condition deterioration accelerates
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 162 THIS WEEK compared to a 44.6 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 263% increase (z-score: 7.19)—suggesting acute pavement failure or pothole formation affecting multiple blocks.
evidence: 162 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 44.6 weekly baseline (263% spike)
z-score of 7.19 indicates highly significant deviation
Correlates with recent snow/ice and weather cycle; may indicate DOT capacity gap
reporting_angles: Document pothole locations with photos; compare complaint map to DOT repair orders.
Interview residents about safety impacts—vehicle damage, pedestrian hazards, accessibility.
Has recent weather (snow/freeze cycle) caused rapid pavement failure? Request DOT response times.

themes_detail.label: Drug activity complaints explode
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints hit 4 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1500% spike (z-score: 8.66)—indicating possible new open-air drug market activity or enforcement shift in the district.
evidence: 4 drug activity complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1500% increase)
z-score of 8.66 indicates extreme statistical significance
Aligns with community board budget request for shelter safety improvement, suggesting adjacent homeless services issues
reporting_angles: Identify specific locations of complaints; interview residents and local business owners about visibility and timing.
Has NYPD stepped up enforcement, or are dealers relocating from other precincts? Request complaint-to-arrest data.
Connect to homeless services: are recent shelter placements correlating with street-level drug activity?

themes_detail.label: Building violations surge unexpectedly
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints jumped to 108 THIS WEEK versus a 28.8 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 276% increase (z-score: 6.62)—suggesting concentrated code violations, illegal conversions, or overcrowding complaints.
evidence: 108 building/use complaints THIS WEEK vs. 28.8 weekly baseline (276% spike)
z-score of 6.62 indicates highly significant deviation
316 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (217 alterations) suggest active construction; complaints may reflect illegal unpermitted work or unsafe conditions
reporting_angles: Analyze complaint types: are they illegal conversions, overcrowded units, or unsafe alterations? Request DOB complaint dataset.
Cross-check against active DOB permits to identify unpermitted work; interview DOB about enforcement capacity.
Community board repeatedly requests 'other expense request for Department of Buildings'—has the district asked for more inspectors?

themes_detail.label: Electrical system complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints spiked to 14 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 3.6 per week—a 286% increase (z-score: 12.11)—indicating potential widespread electrical hazards in buildings or aging infrastructure.
evidence: 14 electrical complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 3.6 weekly average (286% increase)
z-score of 12.11 indicates extreme statistical significance
May relate to aging building stock or increased heating demand in winter season
reporting_angles: Were complaints concentrated in specific blocks or buildings? Request geographic data from 311.
Interview Con Edison about service outages, voltage issues, or infrastructure upgrades in the district.
Check if complaints correlate with the heat/hot water complaints (603 over 90 days)—are residents using illegal heating alternatives?
